from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook

input_path = Path("/mnt/data/spreadsheet/160-6/1_160-6_input.xlsx")
output_path = Path("/mnt/data/outputs/160-6_2_325f0cd8/1_160-6_output.xlsx")
output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# Load the sheet into a DataFrame to identify blank vs non-blank rows.
df = pd.read_excel(input_path, sheet_name="SH", header=0)

# Excel row for the start of the answer range:
start_row = 6
end_row = 11
# Determine which DataFrame rows are completely blank (all NaN)
non_blank_mask = df.notna().any(axis=1)

# We want the non-blank rows that occur at or after the answer range start (i.e., those that
# currently sit below the blank block) to be moved up into the answer range.
# DataFrame row i corresponds to Excel row (i + 2) because header is row 1.
excel_rows = df.index + 2
nonblank_after_mask = non_blank_mask & (excel_rows >= start_row)
nonblank_after = df[nonblank_after_mask].reset_index(drop=True)

# Prepare the list of rows (as lists) to write into A6:L11, starting at row 6.
rows_to_write = nonblank_after.values.tolist()  # each is list of cell values, len == number of columns

# Open workbook and only modify A6:L11
wb = load_workbook(input_path)
ws = wb["SH"]

# Columns A..L -> 1..12
num_cols = 12
write_rows_count = end_row - start_row + 1

for offset in range(write_rows_count):
    excel_r = start_row + offset
    if offset < len(rows_to_write):
        row_values = rows_to_write[offset]
        # Ensure row_values has exactly num_cols entries (if DataFrame had more/less columns, trim/pad)
        # But based on the task, it should match.
        for c in range(1, num_cols + 1):
            val = row_values[c-1] if c-1 < len(row_values) else None
            ws.cell(row=excel_r, column=c).value = None if (pd.isna(val)) else val
    else:
        # Clear remaining cells in the answer range (set to blank)
        for c in range(1, num_cols + 1):
            ws.cell(row=excel_r, column=c).value = None

# Save to the output path
wb.save(output_path)

# Verification: re-open the saved file and print A6:L11 values
wb2 = load_workbook(output_path, data_only=True)
ws2 = wb2["SH"]
result = []
for r in range(start_row, end_row + 1):
    row_vals = []
    for c in range(1, num_cols + 1):
        row_vals.append(ws2.cell(row=r, column=c).value)
    result.append(row_vals)

print("Values written to SH!A6:L11 (rows 6..11):")
